segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Hello, and welcome back to Imagination Nights. [pause 3]

Settle into the bed. Pull the covers up to where you like them. [pause 8]

Take one deep breath, and let it go with a sigh. [pause 8]

Now let your breathing find its own pace. You do not have to control it. Just notice it. [pause 10]

Feel your feet getting heavy. Your legs. Your back sinking into the mattress. [pause 10]

Now let us relax the body, one part at a time. You do not have to do anything. Just notice each part as I name it, and let it get heavy. [pause 8]

Your feet. Let them be warm and heavy. [pause 15]

Your calves and your knees. Heavy. [pause 15]

Your hips and your lower back. Let them sink. [pause 15]

Your belly. Let it rise and fall on its own. [pause 15]

Your chest. Your shoulders. Your arms, all the way down to your fingertips. [pause 15]

Your neck. Your face. The little muscles around your eyes. [pause 15]

Your whole body, heavy and warm, held by the bed. [pause 15]

The day is finished. This part of the night is yours. [pause 8]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Tonight is about a very particular moment. The few minutes just before sleep, when your body is heavy and your thoughts start to drift. [pause 5]

Some people simply call it the drowsy state. It is the moment when you are still awake enough to choose a picture, but relaxed enough that the picture feels real. Arguing and doubting are quieter there. [pause 7]

The practice is simple. Choose one short scene that would happen after your wish comes true. Something that lasts only a few seconds. A handshake. A hug. A sentence someone says to you. [pause 7]

Then, as you get drowsy, you repeat that small scene over and over, gently, like a song you hum to yourself. You do not try hard. You let it loop until you drift off inside it. [pause 7]

Nothing here promises a result. It is a way of ending the day with one hopeful picture instead of a pile of worries. [pause 7]

Choose your small scene now. Something that takes about as long as one breath. [pause 12]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Let your body be heavier than it was a minute ago. Your arms. Your legs. Your eyelids. [pause 14]

Now bring in your small scene. See where you are standing. See who is with you. [pause 14]

Let it happen once. The handshake. The hug. The sentence. Feel it in your hands, or on your face. [pause 17]

Now let it happen again, the same way. No need to make it bigger. [pause 17]

And again. Let it be a little slower this time. [pause 17]

If you lose it, that is all right. Just start it again from the beginning. [pause 17]

Feel how natural it is. As if it has happened many times already. As if it is a memory. [pause 20]

Let the words in the scene become very simple. Maybe just one word. Congratulations. Thank you. Welcome home. [pause 20]

Say that word in your mind, softly, in the rhythm of your breathing. [pause 22]

Notice how little effort this takes. You are not building anything. You are only remembering a moment. [pause 20]

If another thought comes in, let it walk past, like someone crossing the far end of a room. Then come back to your scene. [pause 20]

The handshake. The hug. The words. Again. [pause 22]

Let the scene get smaller and softer, until it fits inside one breath. [pause 22]

Keep looping it as your thoughts get slow. Let the scene and the sleepiness blur together. [pause 27]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
We will end here for tonight. [pause 10]

Keep the feeling, not the effort. Let the effort go. [pause 15]

Whatever happens tomorrow, tonight you practiced feeling at peace. That is worth something on its own. [pause 20]

Let sleep come when it comes. There is no rush. [pause 20]

Notice the weight of the covers. The cool side of the pillow. The dark. [pause 25]

Let each breath out be a little longer than the one before. [pause 25]

Nothing more to picture. Nothing more to try. Only rest. [pause 30]

Good night. [pause 60]

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Teachings in our own words only (living in the end, the drowsy state, revision, a friend's congratulations); no book quoted and the teacher is never named, so no affiliation line is needed; every teaching says plainly it is imagination and feeling, not a promise, and that the real daytime steps still matter ('not a guarantee' reworded so no promise word appears). The love night forbids picturing another person changing their mind and tells anyone in a frightening relationship to reach out for help; revision keeps apologies owed as real; work night pictures bills paid on time, not riches. No God's Word words, journeys or scripture (scripture_woven false).

cultural.note: Warm, plain English for a tired woman at 11 PM; ordinary scenes (porch light, mug, key in the lock, card and pen) with no luxury or wealth fantasy; moving house and long job searches named gently; two settles with a body scan and two closes so nights vary; pacing by silence (18.9-20.4 min).
